title: The Grievance #1: Form 9
author: anonymous
blurb: Photocopied, folded and stapled off-centre by a human being in a hurry. Thirty-two pages about a man whose only power is that he cannot be made to go away. Sold from a bag, not a shelf, for most of its life. The proprietor of Mint Condition keeps every copy he can find and prices them at almost nothing, and will not discuss why.
source: Photocopied linework, high contrast, some pages copied from copies until the greys have gone to solid black or dropped out entirely. Hand-lettered throughout in fine marker. No page numbers. Scanned from the Mint Condition reading copy, Ironside Street, Coldwater. In-universe fiction.

chapters.title: The Whole Thing
chapters.text:
> I am not strong. I have checked.

A municipal corridor. Twelve people deep, running back from a service window under a strip light. He is in the middle of it. Coat. Folder under one arm. Nobody is talking, and the light hums the way that light always hums.

> I am not fast. I am not clever, particularly. I could not lift a car and I would not know what to do with one if I could.

The shutter comes down.

~CLACK~

The queue understands this. The queue has been here before. It comes apart from the front, and the ones at the back leave last because they have the furthest to walk. Then the corridor is empty except for the light, and the man, and the folder.

> I have exactly one thing.

He stays where he is.

> I do not go away.

---

A different day. Same corridor. The queue is back and so is he.

CLERK: The form's been superseded.
MAN: Then give me the one that superseded it.
CLERK: It's not printed yet.
MAN: Then I'll wait.

He steps out of the queue and stands against the wall. He is against that wall when the shift changes. He is against it when the clerk changes. He is against it when they replace the strip light, and you can tell they replaced it, because it is straight now.

> FOURTEEN WEEKS.

A hand comes through the window holding a fresh form. The paper is white. Nothing else on the page is.

> FORM 9.

---

A room with a table. Two people on the other side of it. He is exactly the same size sitting here that he was standing in the queue, which is how he will be drawn until the last page.

OFFICIAL: You understand this doesn't go anywhere.
MAN: It goes to you.
OFFICIAL: And then it goes in a drawer.
MAN: Then it's in a drawer.

OFFICIAL: Do you know how many of these we get?
MAN: No.
OFFICIAL: Nine, last year.
MAN: Nine's not many.
OFFICIAL: Nine is nothing. Nine is a rounding error. Nine is a thing I could lose behind a radiator and nobody would ever ask.

The man does not lean forward. He has not leaned forward once.

MAN: Then it costs you nothing to take it.

The official takes it.

---

Outside. Rain at forty-five degrees straight across everything, the figures included.

A second man waiting under the overhang. Younger. No folder.

SECOND MAN: Did they take it?
MAN: Yes.
SECOND MAN: Does that mean anything?
MAN: No.

They stand in the rain a while.

SECOND MAN: Then why?

Both of them small under a wide sky.

MAN: Because next year it'll be ten.

---

A page of forms, overlapping, dozens of them, filled in by dozens of hands. Some in pen. Some in pencil. One in what is clearly eyeliner.

> IT WAS TEN.

More forms.

> THEN IT WAS FORTY.

Then nothing but forms, layered until the black closes up and there is no white left anywhere.

> THEY PRINTED MORE. THEY HAD TO PRINT MORE. THAT IS ALL. THAT IS THE ENTIRE VICTORY AND I AM AWARE OF HOW IT SOUNDS.

---

The corridor. Empty.

The service window. Shutter down. Taped to the shutter, a printed notice: THIS OFFICE HAS BEEN CLOSED. ENQUIRIES BY POST.

A man standing in front of it with a folder under his arm.

> FINE.

He sits down on the floor against the wall and opens the folder on his knees.

> I HAVE A PEN.

---

> On the back cover, hand-lettered: THIS IS NOT A REAL COMIC AND I AM NOT A REAL ARTIST. I AM A CLERK. I HAVE DRAWN THIS BECAUSE NOBODY READ THE FORM AND I THOUGHT SOMEBODY MIGHT READ A COMIC.

> COPY IT. I MEAN IT. THE WHOLE THING IS DESIGNED TO SURVIVE A PHOTOCOPIER. IF YOU HAVE ACCESS TO A MACHINE AT WORK AND YOU CAN GET AWAY WITH IT, RUN TWENTY AND LEAVE THEM SOMEWHERE.

> DO NOT SELL IT. IF SOMEBODY SOLD YOU THIS, TAKE YOUR MONEY BACK OFF THEM.

> WRITE TO: the address has been blacked out by hand, in every copy anybody has ever found, with a different pen each time.
